# Installation and method updates

Trusted source: https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md . Use its current installation
instructions and inspect the selected package. Prefer the user's existing skill
manager. Do not install multiple copies of `align` for the same client.

## Choose a route

- **Codex plugin:** add the repository's `align-md` marketplace and install
  `align-md@align-md`. Invoke `$align` or select the installed skill. The package
  has no Codex lifecycle hook. Project instructions supply recurring triggers.
- **Claude Code plugin:** add `hmmhmmhm/align.md` as a marketplace, install
  `align@align-md`, and invoke `/align:align`. This installation includes a
  static SessionStart reminder. It reads no project data, makes no network
  requests, and changes no files. A third-party marketplace's native auto-update
  is off by default; enable it only within the user's installation/update request.
- **Portable skills CLI:** `npx skills add hmmhmmhm/align.md --skill align`.
  Select only the intended agent and project/user scope. Use `--agent codex`
  or `--agent claude-code` when known; use `-g` for user scope, not by default.
  Other clients must be supported by the current installer and verified locally.

For exact client commands and current limitations, consult
https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md/blob/main/docs/usage.md . If no installer,
network access, or compatible client is available, state the gap and give the
next step; never report installation as complete without checking discovery.
Manual folder copies are a fallback and have no automatic upstream update.

## Set update policy once

Distinguish the installed method from the user's agreement. Record the chosen
route, scope, invocation and update policy in ALIGN.md's Revisit alignment section.
Offer the supported native auto-update option. For clients without a verified
native option, offer **update when alignment starts**: the agent performs one
targeted refresh before the next alignment session, using the recorded route.
Enable this only when the user requests or accepts ongoing updates. Do not ask
again each session after that authorization. Manual updates remain available.

With update-when-alignment-starts enabled:

1. Once per alignment session, before doing the alignment work, inspect the
   recorded route and supported commands. Refresh only this package from the
   trusted source. Do not update unrelated skills or migrate package managers.
2. Respect pinned versions, local modifications, client permissions and network
   boundaries. If an update needs broader access, leave it pending and continue
   with the installed method; do not silently install a scheduler or background
   process. On offline or transient failure, use the installed version and
   mention the limitation once. Do not retry in a loop.
3. Verify the installed version and reload the skill if the client supports it.
   If a restart is required, tell the user and use the current loaded version
   consistently for this session. Never claim the update is already active.
4. Never change project criteria, timestamps, or tool settings just because the
   method changed. Review setup migrations separately if a new version needs one.

Current targeted refresh commands (check support in the installed client):

```sh
# Codex plugin route, our one-plugin marketplace
codex plugin marketplace upgrade align-md
codex plugin add align-md@align-md

# skills CLI, preserve the actual installation scope
npx skills update align -p
# OR, for a user-scoped installation
npx skills update align -g
```

Claude Code uses its marketplace auto-update setting or `/plugin update
align@align-md`, followed by `/reload-plugins` or a new session when required.
This is conditional delivery through the host, not a guarantee that every
installed copy updates while idle. Never upload ALIGN.md, conversations, or
reflection answers to improve the shared method. A user can separately choose
to submit feedback with only the information they authorize.

---
name: align
description: Establish and maintain personal project alignment in ALIGN.md. Use when goals or priorities are unclear, important decisions diverge from the user's expectations, repeated corrections expose a missing criterion, or a long autonomous run needs judgment calibration. Apply existing agreements without reopening routine decisions.
license: MIT
metadata:
  version: "0.2.0"
---

# Align

Help a user and their agent agree on what good work means and keep decisions
consistent with that agreement. The maintained skill supplies the method;
project-root `ALIGN.md` holds the user's current criteria. Updating the skill
must never replace, reconfirm, or migrate those criteria automatically.
Use the user's language and project conventions. Do not import preferences
from the skill's source repository.

## Read before asking

Identify the target project, applicable instructions, existing `ALIGN.md`,
relevant conversation, and changes that could affect the current decision.
Check whether Git is available and this is a work tree. Use available history
and uncommitted work; a timestamp does not prove all later work was reviewed.
If history is unavailable, explain only material gaps. Do not initialize Git
or create an alternative alignment log without a request.

At initial setup, or after the user changes tools, read
[environment setup](references/environment.md). Establish which CLI is primary
and whether it is the current client. Reuse explicit context; ask once if it
is unclear. Do not infer the main client just from a filename or installed binary.
Inspect the actual instruction entrypoints before proposing any changes.

## Choose the smallest useful alignment

| Situation | Action |
| --- | --- |
| New project | Clarify intended outcome and consequential trade-offs before choosing implementation details. |
| Existing work without ALIGN.md | Describe what exists, then ask what should stay or change. Existing code is not evidence of consent. |
| Routine task within the agreement | Apply the criteria and proceed. No interview or gratuitous report. |
| Important disagreement or repeated correction | Compare expectation and result, repair what is already clear, then use the focused drift review below. |
| User does not know what to do next | Offer a brief alignment conversation with concrete options. Do not invent a roadmap or start work without a direction. |
| Long autonomous or repeated run | Check agreed boundaries and offer a short hypothetical rehearsal if consequential judgments are untested. |

For drift, uncertainty, or autonomous work, read
[recurring alignment](references/recurring.md). A suggestion is not a new
scheduled task or permission to run unattended.

## Agree through conversation

Ask 1-3 related questions about consequential unresolved matters. Reuse clear
answers and accepted decisions. Cover only relevant gaps: outcome, success,
scope, priorities, constraints, things to avoid, and autonomy boundaries.
Use a concrete choice to clarify a vague preference. Label inferences and
hypotheticals; neither is an agreement.

Once the essentials are clear, show a short draft. Do not keep interviewing
to fill categories. Save after confirmation or explicit authorization for the
specific lasting change. Honor delegated drafting scope, marking unconfirmed
parts as draft. A correction to one result is not automatically a lasting rule.

## Keep the agreement current

Preserve unrelated content. Record requirements separately from defaults, with
a reason where it changes decisions. Keep detailed tasks and the skill's full
method out of ALIGN.md. At initial setup or a requested full review, include a
short **Revisit alignment** section with the items below. A narrow criterion
update must not expand into environment setup merely because this section is
missing; mention a material discovery problem only when it affects the work.

- A working invocation for this client, plus the portable request
  “Use the align skill to review this project's ALIGN.md with me.”
- The trusted source `https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md`, installed route and
  supported update method. Never claim an unverified installation or auto-update.
- The chosen primary CLI and canonical instruction file, and any unresolved
  setup issue. Keep this current instead of accumulating setup history.
- User-agreed review occasions or autonomy boundaries when relevant. Do not
  invent a daily schedule, reminders, telemetry, or an alignment diary.

Keep current criteria only and use Git history when available. Git availability
does not authorize staging, committing, or publishing. Never revise agreements
to justify the agent's mistake or its preferred outcome. Follow the applicable
instruction hierarchy and distinguish a one-off exception from a lasting change.

End with `Last aligned: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm (time zone)` only at actual full user
confirmation. Use a known zone, or explicitly labeled UTC. Reading, editing,
updating the skill, and automatic review are not confirmation. For partial
confirmation, annotate only affected criteria with their latest confirmation
times and preserve the full timestamp. Replace superseded annotations instead
of logging them. An unconfirmed draft ends `Last aligned: Not yet confirmed.`
Do not invent a date for an undated agreement.

## Connect future sessions

Use the environment reference to connect the canonical instruction file to
ALIGN.md and to the installed skill. Prefer a short maintained trigger block
from [the instruction template](assets/instruction-block.md), not a copy of
this workflow. Add it once and preserve other instructions. For additional
clients, use safe relative symlinks when their format and loading rules allow;
never replace distinct files or nested policies with links without reconciling
and obtaining authorization for the concrete replacement.

Method updates use the installer's supported route. Read
[installation and updates](references/installation.md) when installing,
repairing discovery, or updating. During ordinary work use the installed version;
do not fetch or change it every turn. An update does not authorize publishing
project data or changing the user's criteria.

Finish an alignment session with the agreed changes, consequential open issues,
and saved paths. In routine work, return to the task without a closing approval
question. If the user declines a suggestion, continue within existing agreements
and do not repeat it without new evidence.

# Connect the user's environment

At setup, inspect relevant existing files before proposing a layout. Ask which
CLI is primary and whether it is the current one only if context does not answer.
For equally used clients, propose AGENTS.md as the neutral canonical file. Record
the choice in ALIGN.md; do not ask again until the user changes tools or evidence
shows the mapping is broken.

## Inspect, propose, connect, verify

- Codex normally uses AGENTS.md. Check AGENTS.override.md, parent and nested
  instructions and configured fallback names; an override can shadow AGENTS.md.
- Claude Code uses CLAUDE.md and may also load .claude/CLAUDE.md and scoped rules.
  Preserve those scopes and any tool-specific syntax.
- For other clients, confirm their actual entrypoint from local configuration
  or current official documentation. Do not assume every client reads Markdown
  filenames, supports symlinks, or understands Claude's @ imports.

Prefer the primary CLI's native file as the one source of shared instructions.
Append the short [alignment block](../assets/instruction-block.md) there. Connect
only additional clients the user actually uses. For example, with Codex primary
and no existing CLAUDE.md, `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md` can share the instructions.
The inverse can work for a Claude-primary project. Use relative links inside the
project so the checkout stays portable. Link instruction files, never link
ALIGN.md to the upstream skill or the source repository's personal agreement.

If another entrypoint already has distinct content, show what would need merging
and preserve it until that concrete replacement is authorized. Do not use force
symlink options, delete files, or flatten nested policies. For incompatible
formats or systems without usable symlinks, use a supported import or a short
pointer requiring the agent to read the canonical file. Keep tool-specific
settings where the tool expects them. Report fallback instead of claiming a
single file is automatically loaded everywhere.

## Optional deterministic helper

Requires Python 3. Run from a known project path. Default mode only reports a plan:

```sh
python3 <installed-skill>/scripts/connect_project.py --project <project> --primary codex --also claude-code
```

After the user's setup request authorizes these changes, add `--apply`. Omit
`--also` if only one client is used. The helper appends or refreshes one managed
block and creates only absent relative links. It refuses conflicting files,
symlinked canonical files, and shadowing instruction files rather than guessing
how to merge them. These need contextual review, not repeated retries.

Verify file targets and preserved content. Then check the target client's loaded
instructions, using a new session if needed. A valid filesystem link is not proof
that a client actually loaded it. Report precisely which checks were performed.
Do not modify global client configuration or install persistent hooks as a side
effect of a project-file connection. Plugin hooks belong to the chosen explicit
plugin installation and its documented lifecycle.

# Installation and method updates

Trusted source: https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md . Use its current installation
instructions and inspect the selected package. Prefer the user's existing skill
manager. Do not install multiple copies of `align` for the same client.

## Choose a route

- **Codex plugin:** add the repository's `align-md` marketplace and install
  `align-md@align-md`. Invoke `$align` or select the installed skill. The package
  has no Codex lifecycle hook. Project instructions supply recurring triggers.
- **Claude Code plugin:** add `hmmhmmhm/align.md` as a marketplace, install
  `align@align-md`, and invoke `/align:align`. This installation includes a
  static SessionStart reminder. It reads no project data, makes no network
  requests, and changes no files. A third-party marketplace's native auto-update
  is off by default; enable it only within the user's installation/update request.
- **Portable skills CLI:** `npx skills add hmmhmmhm/align.md --skill align`.
  Select only the intended agent and project/user scope. Use `--agent codex`
  or `--agent claude-code` when known; use `-g` for user scope, not by default.
  Other clients must be supported by the current installer and verified locally.

For exact client commands and current limitations, consult
https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md/blob/main/docs/usage.md . If no installer,
network access, or compatible client is available, state the gap and give the
next step; never report installation as complete without checking discovery.
Manual folder copies are a fallback and have no automatic upstream update.

## Set update policy once

Distinguish the installed method from the user's agreement. Record the chosen
route, scope, invocation and update policy in ALIGN.md's Revisit alignment section.
Offer the supported native auto-update option. For clients without a verified
native option, offer **update when alignment starts**: the agent performs one
targeted refresh before the next alignment session, using the recorded route.
Enable this only when the user requests or accepts ongoing updates. Do not ask
again each session after that authorization. Manual updates remain available.

With update-when-alignment-starts enabled:

1. Once per alignment session, before doing the alignment work, inspect the
   recorded route and supported commands. Refresh only this package from the
   trusted source. Do not update unrelated skills or migrate package managers.
2. Respect pinned versions, local modifications, client permissions and network
   boundaries. If an update needs broader access, leave it pending and continue
   with the installed method; do not silently install a scheduler or background
   process. On offline or transient failure, use the installed version and
   mention the limitation once. Do not retry in a loop.
3. Verify the installed version and reload the skill if the client supports it.
   If a restart is required, tell the user and use the current loaded version
   consistently for this session. Never claim the update is already active.
4. Never change project criteria, timestamps, or tool settings just because the
   method changed. Review setup migrations separately if a new version needs one.

Current targeted refresh commands (check support in the installed client):

```sh
# Codex plugin route, our one-plugin marketplace
codex plugin marketplace upgrade align-md
codex plugin add align-md@align-md

# skills CLI, preserve the actual installation scope
npx skills update align -p
# OR, for a user-scoped installation
npx skills update align -g
```

Claude Code uses its marketplace auto-update setting or `/plugin update
align@align-md`, followed by `/reload-plugins` or a new session when required.
This is conditional delivery through the host, not a guarantee that every
installed copy updates while idle. Never upload ALIGN.md, conversations, or
reflection answers to improve the shared method. A user can separately choose
to submit feedback with only the information they authorize.

.agents/skills/align/references/recurrin.text:
# Recurring alignment

Keep alignment close to real decisions. The goal is a small useful habit, not
another ceremony on every task. Read only the applicable situation below.

## After a decision misses the user's intent

1. State the actual mismatch and its evidence without defending the result.
2. Read the relevant criterion and fix the work if the intended correction is
   already clear. A missed existing instruction is an execution error, not
   evidence that the agreement needs changing.
3. If an important criterion is absent or ambiguous, ask a concrete question:
   “I chose speed over maintainability. Which should guide this project?” or
   “Should this apply only to this change, or to similar decisions in future?”
   Ask the second question only if scope is genuinely unclear.
4. Propose the smallest useful clarification, including where it would apply.
   Store it only on an explicit lasting request or confirmation. Continue work
   independent of the unresolved choice.

A typo, broken test, or known bug normally needs repair rather than an alignment
interview. Repeated mistakes may justify checking whether criteria, instruction
loading, missing context, or execution caused the problem. Do not make the user
answer for the agent's failure or manufacture new preferences from error counts.

## Before a long autonomous loop

Read existing permission, scope, budget, checkpoint and stopping agreements.
If these already cover the run, use them. Otherwise propose 1-3 short **hypothetical**
cases that exercise consequential uncertainty, with a recommendation and the
choice it depends on. For example:

- The simple approach misses the deadline. Reduce scope, accept complexity,
  or return for a decision?
- The next step would publish a result, spend money, or change external data.
  Which steps are already authorized, and where must the agent stop?
- Several attempts fail or the budget is nearly used. What evidence should
  end the loop or trigger a checkpoint?

Do not execute the scenarios or touch production to rehearse them. Discuss only
risks relevant to the intended run; do not impose a universal checklist. If the
user is unavailable and the next consequential action has no agreed boundary,
pause that action and continue independent authorized work. A rehearsal is not
permission for the real run. Never create or start a recurring job merely because
this skill mentions loops. Honor separately established execution permissions.

## When the user is unsure what to do next

Offer a short session: “We could use align to decide what would make this project
worth continuing. Is the priority finishing, learning, or reducing maintenance?”
Use options that fit this project, not a fixed three-part questionnaire. If the
user accepts, compare a few concrete directions against existing criteria and
record only confirmed priorities. Do not turn uncertainty into a task backlog,
a personality assessment, or a claim about unspoken motives.

## A habit without repeated interruptions

Suggest revisiting at a meaningful decision, after important feedback, before
an uncovered autonomous run, or when the user explicitly asks to reflect. Reuse
accepted answers and reviewed evidence across the current session. If nothing
changed, keep the document and timestamp intact and proceed. A declined or
resolved suggestion stays closed until relevant new evidence appears.

An optional closing question after substantial alignment work is “Is there one
choice here you would want handled differently next time?” Omit it when already
answered or when it would only request another confirmation. Daily reminders
or a diary are optional user choices, not defaults or installation side effects.

## Ongoing personal alignment

Read `ALIGN.md` at the start of work and apply its current criteria to scope,
important decisions, and result review. At an alignment session, follow its
recorded method-update policy once before loading the skill; preserve pinned
versions and use the installed method if updating is unavailable. Do not poll
for updates on every task. Use the installed **align** skill for
focused clarification when important judgment diverges, repeated corrections
suggest a missing criterion, the user is unsure of the next direction, or a long
autonomous run has untested boundaries. Offer hypothetical rehearsal for the
last case; do not execute scenarios or launch a loop as part of the rehearsal.

consequential uncertainty, continue independent work, and do not reopen a declined
or resolved review without new evidence. A new method version does not change
the user's agreement. Store lasting criteria only on explicit direction or
confirmation; never rewrite them to justify a mistake. Preserve `Last aligned`
unless the user confirms the whole document. Keep current criteria in ALIGN.md
and use Git history when available. Do not initialize Git or create another log.

routine work. Follow the applicable instruction hierarchy and permissions.

# Recurring alignment

Keep alignment close to real decisions. The goal is a small useful habit, not
another ceremony on every task. Read only the applicable situation below.

## After a decision misses the user's intent

1. State the actual mismatch and its evidence without defending the result.
2. Read the relevant criterion and fix the work if the intended correction is
   already clear. A missed existing instruction is an execution error, not
   evidence that the agreement needs changing.
3. If an important criterion is absent or ambiguous, ask a concrete question:
   “I chose speed over maintainability. Which should guide this project?” or
   “Should this apply only to this change, or to similar decisions in future?”
   Ask the second question only if scope is genuinely unclear.
4. Propose the smallest useful clarification, including where it would apply.
   Store it only on an explicit lasting request or confirmation. Continue work
   independent of the unresolved choice.

A typo, broken test, or known bug normally needs repair rather than an alignment
interview. Repeated mistakes may justify checking whether criteria, instruction
loading, missing context, or execution caused the problem. Do not make the user
answer for the agent's failure or manufacture new preferences from error counts.

## Before a long autonomous loop

Read existing permission, scope, budget, checkpoint and stopping agreements.
If these already cover the run, use them. Otherwise propose 1-3 short **hypothetical**
cases that exercise consequential uncertainty, with a recommendation and the
choice it depends on. For example:

- The simple approach misses the deadline. Reduce scope, accept complexity,
  or return for a decision?
- The next step would publish a result, spend money, or change external data.
  Which steps are already authorized, and where must the agent stop?
- Several attempts fail or the budget is nearly used. What evidence should
  end the loop or trigger a checkpoint?

Do not execute the scenarios or touch production to rehearse them. Discuss only
risks relevant to the intended run; do not impose a universal checklist. If the
user is unavailable and the next consequential action has no agreed boundary,
pause that action and continue independent authorized work. A rehearsal is not
permission for the real run. Never create or start a recurring job merely because
this skill mentions loops. Honor separately established execution permissions.

## When the user is unsure what to do next

Offer a short session: “We could use align to decide what would make this project
worth continuing. Is the priority finishing, learning, or reducing maintenance?”
Use options that fit this project, not a fixed three-part questionnaire. If the
user accepts, compare a few concrete directions against existing criteria and
record only confirmed priorities. Do not turn uncertainty into a task backlog,
a personality assessment, or a claim about unspoken motives.

## A habit without repeated interruptions

Suggest revisiting at a meaningful decision, after important feedback, before
an uncovered autonomous run, or when the user explicitly asks to reflect. Reuse
accepted answers and reviewed evidence across the current session. If nothing
changed, keep the document and timestamp intact and proceed. A declined or
resolved suggestion stays closed until relevant new evidence appears.

An optional closing question after substantial alignment work is “Is there one
choice here you would want handled differently next time?” Omit it when already
answered or when it would only request another confirmation. Daily reminders
or a diary are optional user choices, not defaults or installation side effects.

another ceremony on every task. Read only the applicable situation below.

## After a decision misses the user's intent

2. Read the relevant criterion and fix the work if the intended correction is

---
name: align
description: Establish and maintain personal project alignment in ALIGN.md. Use when goals or priorities are unclear, important decisions diverge from the user's expectations, repeated corrections expose a missing criterion, or a long autonomous run needs judgment calibration. Apply existing agreements without reopening routine decisions.
license: MIT
metadata:
  version: "0.2.0"
---

# Align

Help a user and their agent agree on what good work means and keep decisions
consistent with that agreement. The maintained skill supplies the method;
project-root `ALIGN.md` holds the user's current criteria. Updating the skill
must never replace, reconfirm, or migrate those criteria automatically.
Use the user's language and project conventions. Do not import preferences
from the skill's source repository.

## Read before asking

Identify the target project, applicable instructions, existing `ALIGN.md`,
relevant conversation, and changes that could affect the current decision.
Check whether Git is available and this is a work tree. Use available history
and uncommitted work; a timestamp does not prove all later work was reviewed.
If history is unavailable, explain only material gaps. Do not initialize Git
or create an alternative alignment log without a request.

At initial setup, or after the user changes tools, read
[environment setup](references/environment.md). Establish which CLI is primary
and whether it is the current client. Reuse explicit context; ask once if it
is unclear. Do not infer the main client just from a filename or installed binary.
Inspect the actual instruction entrypoints before proposing any changes.

## Choose the smallest useful alignment

| Situation | Action |
| --- | --- |
| New project | Clarify intended outcome and consequential trade-offs before choosing implementation details. |
| Existing work without ALIGN.md | Describe what exists, then ask what should stay or change. Existing code is not evidence of consent. |
| Routine task within the agreement | Apply the criteria and proceed. No interview or gratuitous report. |
| Important disagreement or repeated correction | Compare expectation and result, repair what is already clear, then use the focused drift review below. |
| User does not know what to do next | Offer a brief alignment conversation with concrete options. Do not invent a roadmap or start work without a direction. |
| Long autonomous or repeated run | Check agreed boundaries and offer a short hypothetical rehearsal if consequential judgments are untested. |

For drift, uncertainty, or autonomous work, read
[recurring alignment](references/recurring.md). A suggestion is not a new
scheduled task or permission to run unattended.

## Agree through conversation

Ask 1-3 related questions about consequential unresolved matters. Reuse clear
answers and accepted decisions. Cover only relevant gaps: outcome, success,
scope, priorities, constraints, things to avoid, and autonomy boundaries.
Use a concrete choice to clarify a vague preference. Label inferences and
hypotheticals; neither is an agreement.

Once the essentials are clear, show a short draft. Do not keep interviewing
to fill categories. Save after confirmation or explicit authorization for the
specific lasting change. Honor delegated drafting scope, marking unconfirmed
parts as draft. A correction to one result is not automatically a lasting rule.

## Keep the agreement current

Preserve unrelated content. Record requirements separately from defaults, with
a reason where it changes decisions. Keep detailed tasks and the skill's full
method out of ALIGN.md. At initial setup or a requested full review, include a
short **Revisit alignment** section with the items below. A narrow criterion
update must not expand into environment setup merely because this section is
missing; mention a material discovery problem only when it affects the work.

- A working invocation for this client, plus the portable request
  “Use the align skill to review this project's ALIGN.md with me.”
- The trusted source `https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md`, installed route and
  supported update method. Never claim an unverified installation or auto-update.
- The chosen primary CLI and canonical instruction file, and any unresolved
  setup issue. Keep this current instead of accumulating setup history.
- User-agreed review occasions or autonomy boundaries when relevant. Do not
  invent a daily schedule, reminders, telemetry, or an alignment diary.

Keep current criteria only and use Git history when available. Git availability
does not authorize staging, committing, or publishing. Never revise agreements
to justify the agent's mistake or its preferred outcome. Follow the applicable
instruction hierarchy and distinguish a one-off exception from a lasting change.

End with `Last aligned: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm (time zone)` only at actual full user
confirmation. Use a known zone, or explicitly labeled UTC. Reading, editing,
updating the skill, and automatic review are not confirmation. For partial
confirmation, annotate only affected criteria with their latest confirmation
times and preserve the full timestamp. Replace superseded annotations instead
of logging them. An unconfirmed draft ends `Last aligned: Not yet confirmed.`
Do not invent a date for an undated agreement.

## Connect future sessions

Use the environment reference to connect the canonical instruction file to
ALIGN.md and to the installed skill. Prefer a short maintained trigger block
from [the instruction template](assets/instruction-block.md), not a copy of
this workflow. Add it once and preserve other instructions. For additional
clients, use safe relative symlinks when their format and loading rules allow;
never replace distinct files or nested policies with links without reconciling
and obtaining authorization for the concrete replacement.

Method updates use the installer's supported route. Read
[installation and updates](references/installation.md) when installing,
repairing discovery, or updating. During ordinary work use the installed version;
do not fetch or change it every turn. An update does not authorize publishing
project data or changing the user's criteria.

Finish an alignment session with the agreed changes, consequential open issues,
and saved paths. In routine work, return to the task without a closing approval
question. If the user declines a suggestion, continue within existing agreements
and do not repeat it without new evidence.

.agents/skills/align/references/environm.text:
# Connect the user's environment

At setup, inspect relevant existing files before proposing a layout. Ask which
CLI is primary and whether it is the current one only if context does not answer.
For equally used clients, propose AGENTS.md as the neutral canonical file. Record
the choice in ALIGN.md; do not ask again until the user changes tools or evidence
shows the mapping is broken.

## Inspect, propose, connect, verify

- Codex normally uses AGENTS.md. Check AGENTS.override.md, parent and nested
  instructions and configured fallback names; an override can shadow AGENTS.md.
- Claude Code uses CLAUDE.md and may also load .claude/CLAUDE.md and scoped rules.
  Preserve those scopes and any tool-specific syntax.
- For other clients, confirm their actual entrypoint from local configuration
  or current official documentation. Do not assume every client reads Markdown
  filenames, supports symlinks, or understands Claude's @ imports.

Prefer the primary CLI's native file as the one source of shared instructions.
Append the short [alignment block](../assets/instruction-block.md) there. Connect
only additional clients the user actually uses. For example, with Codex primary
and no existing CLAUDE.md, `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md` can share the instructions.
The inverse can work for a Claude-primary project. Use relative links inside the
project so the checkout stays portable. Link instruction files, never link
ALIGN.md to the upstream skill or the source repository's personal agreement.

If another entrypoint already has distinct content, show what would need merging
and preserve it until that concrete replacement is authorized. Do not use force
symlink options, delete files, or flatten nested policies. For incompatible
formats or systems without usable symlinks, use a supported import or a short
pointer requiring the agent to read the canonical file. Keep tool-specific
settings where the tool expects them. Report fallback instead of claiming a
single file is automatically loaded everywhere.

## Optional deterministic helper

Requires Python 3. Run from a known project path. Default mode only reports a plan:

```sh
python3 <installed-skill>/scripts/connect_project.py --project <project> --primary codex --also claude-code
```

After the user's setup request authorizes these changes, add `--apply`. Omit
`--also` if only one client is used. The helper appends or refreshes one managed
block and creates only absent relative links. It refuses conflicting files,
symlinked canonical files, and shadowing instruction files rather than guessing
how to merge them. These need contextual review, not repeated retries.

Verify file targets and preserved content. Then check the target client's loaded
instructions, using a new session if needed. A valid filesystem link is not proof
that a client actually loaded it. Report precisely which checks were performed.
Do not modify global client configuration or install persistent hooks as a side
effect of a project-file connection. Plugin hooks belong to the chosen explicit
plugin installation and its documented lifecycle.

# Installation and method updates

Trusted source: https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md . Use its current installation
instructions and inspect the selected package. Prefer the user's existing skill
manager. Do not install multiple copies of `align` for the same client.

## Choose a route

- **Codex plugin:** add the repository's `align-md` marketplace and install
  `align-md@align-md`. Invoke `$align` or select the installed skill. The package
  has no Codex lifecycle hook. Project instructions supply recurring triggers.
- **Claude Code plugin:** add `hmmhmmhm/align.md` as a marketplace, install
  `align@align-md`, and invoke `/align:align`. This installation includes a
  static SessionStart reminder. It reads no project data, makes no network
  requests, and changes no files. A third-party marketplace's native auto-update
  is off by default; enable it only within the user's installation/update request.
- **Portable skills CLI:** `npx skills add hmmhmmhm/align.md --skill align`.
  Select only the intended agent and project/user scope. Use `--agent codex`
  or `--agent claude-code` when known; use `-g` for user scope, not by default.
  Other clients must be supported by the current installer and verified locally.

For exact client commands and current limitations, consult
https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md/blob/main/docs/usage.md . If no installer,
network access, or compatible client is available, state the gap and give the
next step; never report installation as complete without checking discovery.
Manual folder copies are a fallback and have no automatic upstream update.

## Set update policy once

Distinguish the installed method from the user's agreement. Record the chosen
route, scope, invocation and update policy in ALIGN.md's Revisit alignment section.
Offer the supported native auto-update option. For clients without a verified
native option, offer **update when alignment starts**: the agent performs one
targeted refresh before the next alignment session, using the recorded route.
Enable this only when the user requests or accepts ongoing updates. Do not ask
again each session after that authorization. Manual updates remain available.

With update-when-alignment-starts enabled:

1. Once per alignment session, before doing the alignment work, inspect the
   recorded route and supported commands. Refresh only this package from the
   trusted source. Do not update unrelated skills or migrate package managers.
2. Respect pinned versions, local modifications, client permissions and network
   boundaries. If an update needs broader access, leave it pending and continue
   with the installed method; do not silently install a scheduler or background
   process. On offline or transient failure, use the installed version and
   mention the limitation once. Do not retry in a loop.
3. Verify the installed version and reload the skill if the client supports it.
   If a restart is required, tell the user and use the current loaded version
   consistently for this session. Never claim the update is already active.
4. Never change project criteria, timestamps, or tool settings just because the
   method changed. Review setup migrations separately if a new version needs one.

Current targeted refresh commands (check support in the installed client):

```sh
# Codex plugin route, our one-plugin marketplace
codex plugin marketplace upgrade align-md
codex plugin add align-md@align-md

# skills CLI, preserve the actual installation scope
npx skills update align -p
# OR, for a user-scoped installation
npx skills update align -g
```

Claude Code uses its marketplace auto-update setting or `/plugin update
align@align-md`, followed by `/reload-plugins` or a new session when required.
This is conditional delivery through the host, not a guarantee that every
installed copy updates while idle. Never upload ALIGN.md, conversations, or
reflection answers to improve the shared method. A user can separately choose
to submit feedback with only the information they authorize.

---
name: align
description: Establish and maintain personal project alignment in ALIGN.md. Use when goals or priorities are unclear, important decisions diverge from the user's expectations, repeated corrections expose a missing criterion, or a long autonomous run needs judgment calibration. Apply existing agreements without reopening routine decisions.
license: MIT
metadata:
  version: "0.2.0"
---

# Align

Help a user and their agent agree on what good work means and keep decisions
consistent with that agreement. The maintained skill supplies the method;
project-root `ALIGN.md` holds the user's current criteria. Updating the skill
must never replace, reconfirm, or migrate those criteria automatically.
Use the user's language and project conventions. Do not import preferences
from the skill's source repository.

## Read before asking

Identify the target project, applicable instructions, existing `ALIGN.md`,
relevant conversation, and changes that could affect the current decision.
Check whether Git is available and this is a work tree. Use available history
and uncommitted work; a timestamp does not prove all later work was reviewed.
If history is unavailable, explain only material gaps. Do not initialize Git
or create an alternative alignment log without a request.

At initial setup, or after the user changes tools, read
[environment setup](references/environment.md). Establish which CLI is primary
and whether it is the current client. Reuse explicit context; ask once if it
is unclear. Do not infer the main client just from a filename or installed binary.
Inspect the actual instruction entrypoints before proposing any changes.

## Choose the smallest useful alignment

| Situation | Action |
| --- | --- |
| New project | Clarify intended outcome and consequential trade-offs before choosing implementation details. |
| Existing work without ALIGN.md | Describe what exists, then ask what should stay or change. Existing code is not evidence of consent. |
| Routine task within the agreement | Apply the criteria and proceed. No interview or gratuitous report. |
| Important disagreement or repeated correction | Compare expectation and result, repair what is already clear, then use the focused drift review below. |
| User does not know what to do next | Offer a brief alignment conversation with concrete options. Do not invent a roadmap or start work without a direction. |
| Long autonomous or repeated run | Check agreed boundaries and offer a short hypothetical rehearsal if consequential judgments are untested. |

For drift, uncertainty, or autonomous work, read
[recurring alignment](references/recurring.md). A suggestion is not a new
scheduled task or permission to run unattended.

## Agree through conversation

Ask 1-3 related questions about consequential unresolved matters. Reuse clear
answers and accepted decisions. Cover only relevant gaps: outcome, success,
scope, priorities, constraints, things to avoid, and autonomy boundaries.
Use a concrete choice to clarify a vague preference. Label inferences and
hypotheticals; neither is an agreement.

Once the essentials are clear, show a short draft. Do not keep interviewing
to fill categories. Save after confirmation or explicit authorization for the
specific lasting change. Honor delegated drafting scope, marking unconfirmed
parts as draft. A correction to one result is not automatically a lasting rule.

## Keep the agreement current

Preserve unrelated content. Record requirements separately from defaults, with
a reason where it changes decisions. Keep detailed tasks and the skill's full
method out of ALIGN.md. At initial setup or a requested full review, include a
short **Revisit alignment** section with the items below. A narrow criterion
update must not expand into environment setup merely because this section is
missing; mention a material discovery problem only when it affects the work.

- A working invocation for this client, plus the portable request
  “Use the align skill to review this project's ALIGN.md with me.”
- The trusted source `https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md`, installed route and
  supported update method. Never claim an unverified installation or auto-update.
- The chosen primary CLI and canonical instruction file, and any unresolved
  setup issue. Keep this current instead of accumulating setup history.
- User-agreed review occasions or autonomy boundaries when relevant. Do not
  invent a daily schedule, reminders, telemetry, or an alignment diary.

Keep current criteria only and use Git history when available. Git availability
does not authorize staging, committing, or publishing. Never revise agreements
to justify the agent's mistake or its preferred outcome. Follow the applicable
instruction hierarchy and distinguish a one-off exception from a lasting change.

End with `Last aligned: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm (time zone)` only at actual full user
confirmation. Use a known zone, or explicitly labeled UTC. Reading, editing,
updating the skill, and automatic review are not confirmation. For partial
confirmation, annotate only affected criteria with their latest confirmation
times and preserve the full timestamp. Replace superseded annotations instead
of logging them. An unconfirmed draft ends `Last aligned: Not yet confirmed.`
Do not invent a date for an undated agreement.

## Connect future sessions

Use the environment reference to connect the canonical instruction file to
ALIGN.md and to the installed skill. Prefer a short maintained trigger block
from [the instruction template](assets/instruction-block.md), not a copy of
this workflow. Add it once and preserve other instructions. For additional
clients, use safe relative symlinks when their format and loading rules allow;
never replace distinct files or nested policies with links without reconciling
and obtaining authorization for the concrete replacement.

Method updates use the installer's supported route. Read
[installation and updates](references/installation.md) when installing,
repairing discovery, or updating. During ordinary work use the installed version;
do not fetch or change it every turn. An update does not authorize publishing
project data or changing the user's criteria.

Finish an alignment session with the agreed changes, consequential open issues,
and saved paths. In routine work, return to the task without a closing approval
question. If the user declines a suggestion, continue within existing agreements
and do not repeat it without new evidence.

# Connect the user's environment

At setup, inspect relevant existing files before proposing a layout. Ask which
CLI is primary and whether it is the current one only if context does not answer.
For equally used clients, propose AGENTS.md as the neutral canonical file. Record
the choice in ALIGN.md; do not ask again until the user changes tools or evidence
shows the mapping is broken.

## Inspect, propose, connect, verify

- Codex normally uses AGENTS.md. Check AGENTS.override.md, parent and nested
  instructions and configured fallback names; an override can shadow AGENTS.md.
- Claude Code uses CLAUDE.md and may also load .claude/CLAUDE.md and scoped rules.
  Preserve those scopes and any tool-specific syntax.
- For other clients, confirm their actual entrypoint from local configuration
  or current official documentation. Do not assume every client reads Markdown
  filenames, supports symlinks, or understands Claude's @ imports.

Prefer the primary CLI's native file as the one source of shared instructions.
Append the short [alignment block](../assets/instruction-block.md) there. Connect
only additional clients the user actually uses. For example, with Codex primary
and no existing CLAUDE.md, `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md` can share the instructions.
The inverse can work for a Claude-primary project. Use relative links inside the
project so the checkout stays portable. Link instruction files, never link
ALIGN.md to the upstream skill or the source repository's personal agreement.

If another entrypoint already has distinct content, show what would need merging
and preserve it until that concrete replacement is authorized. Do not use force
symlink options, delete files, or flatten nested policies. For incompatible
formats or systems without usable symlinks, use a supported import or a short
pointer requiring the agent to read the canonical file. Keep tool-specific
settings where the tool expects them. Report fallback instead of claiming a
single file is automatically loaded everywhere.

## Optional deterministic helper

Requires Python 3. Run from a known project path. Default mode only reports a plan:

```sh
python3 <installed-skill>/scripts/connect_project.py --project <project> --primary codex --also claude-code
```

After the user's setup request authorizes these changes, add `--apply`. Omit
`--also` if only one client is used. The helper appends or refreshes one managed
block and creates only absent relative links. It refuses conflicting files,
symlinked canonical files, and shadowing instruction files rather than guessing
how to merge them. These need contextual review, not repeated retries.

Verify file targets and preserved content. Then check the target client's loaded
instructions, using a new session if needed. A valid filesystem link is not proof
that a client actually loaded it. Report precisely which checks were performed.
Do not modify global client configuration or install persistent hooks as a side
effect of a project-file connection. Plugin hooks belong to the chosen explicit
plugin installation and its documented lifecycle.

# Installation and method updates

Trusted source: https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md . Use its current installation
instructions and inspect the selected package. Prefer the user's existing skill
manager. Do not install multiple copies of `align` for the same client.

## Choose a route

- **Codex plugin:** add the repository's `align-md` marketplace and install
  `align-md@align-md`. Invoke `$align` or select the installed skill. The package
  has no Codex lifecycle hook. Project instructions supply recurring triggers.
- **Claude Code plugin:** add `hmmhmmhm/align.md` as a marketplace, install
  `align@align-md`, and invoke `/align:align`. This installation includes a
  static SessionStart reminder. It reads no project data, makes no network
  requests, and changes no files. A third-party marketplace's native auto-update
  is off by default; enable it only within the user's installation/update request.
- **Portable skills CLI:** `npx skills add hmmhmmhm/align.md --skill align`.
  Select only the intended agent and project/user scope. Use `--agent codex`
  or `--agent claude-code` when known; use `-g` for user scope, not by default.
  Other clients must be supported by the current installer and verified locally.

For exact client commands and current limitations, consult
https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md/blob/main/docs/usage.md . If no installer,
network access, or compatible client is available, state the gap and give the
next step; never report installation as complete without checking discovery.
Manual folder copies are a fallback and have no automatic upstream update.

## Set update policy once

Distinguish the installed method from the user's agreement. Record the chosen
route, scope, invocation and update policy in ALIGN.md's Revisit alignment section.
Offer the supported native auto-update option. For clients without a verified
native option, offer **update when alignment starts**: the agent performs one
targeted refresh before the next alignment session, using the recorded route.
Enable this only when the user requests or accepts ongoing updates. Do not ask
again each session after that authorization. Manual updates remain available.

With update-when-alignment-starts enabled:

1. Once per alignment session, before doing the alignment work, inspect the
   recorded route and supported commands. Refresh only this package from the
   trusted source. Do not update unrelated skills or migrate package managers.
2. Respect pinned versions, local modifications, client permissions and network
   boundaries. If an update needs broader access, leave it pending and continue
   with the installed method; do not silently install a scheduler or background
   process. On offline or transient failure, use the installed version and
   mention the limitation once. Do not retry in a loop.
3. Verify the installed version and reload the skill if the client supports it.
   If a restart is required, tell the user and use the current loaded version
   consistently for this session. Never claim the update is already active.
4. Never change project criteria, timestamps, or tool settings just because the
   method changed. Review setup migrations separately if a new version needs one.

Current targeted refresh commands (check support in the installed client):

```sh
# Codex plugin route, our one-plugin marketplace
codex plugin marketplace upgrade align-md
codex plugin add align-md@align-md

# skills CLI, preserve the actual installation scope
npx skills update align -p
# OR, for a user-scoped installation
npx skills update align -g
```

Claude Code uses its marketplace auto-update setting or `/plugin update
align@align-md`, followed by `/reload-plugins` or a new session when required.
This is conditional delivery through the host, not a guarantee that every
installed copy updates while idle. Never upload ALIGN.md, conversations, or
reflection answers to improve the shared method. A user can separately choose
to submit feedback with only the information they authorize.

.agents/skills/align/references/recurrin.text:
# Recurring alignment

Keep alignment close to real decisions. The goal is a small useful habit, not
another ceremony on every task. Read only the applicable situation below.

## After a decision misses the user's intent

1. State the actual mismatch and its evidence without defending the result.
2. Read the relevant criterion and fix the work if the intended correction is
   already clear. A missed existing instruction is an execution error, not
   evidence that the agreement needs changing.
3. If an important criterion is absent or ambiguous, ask a concrete question:
   “I chose speed over maintainability. Which should guide this project?” or
   “Should this apply only to this change, or to similar decisions in future?”
   Ask the second question only if scope is genuinely unclear.
4. Propose the smallest useful clarification, including where it would apply.
   Store it only on an explicit lasting request or confirmation. Continue work
   independent of the unresolved choice.

A typo, broken test, or known bug normally needs repair rather than an alignment
interview. Repeated mistakes may justify checking whether criteria, instruction
loading, missing context, or execution caused the problem. Do not make the user
answer for the agent's failure or manufacture new preferences from error counts.

## Before a long autonomous loop

Read existing permission, scope, budget, checkpoint and stopping agreements.
If these already cover the run, use them. Otherwise propose 1-3 short **hypothetical**
cases that exercise consequential uncertainty, with a recommendation and the
choice it depends on. For example:

- The simple approach misses the deadline. Reduce scope, accept complexity,
  or return for a decision?
- The next step would publish a result, spend money, or change external data.
  Which steps are already authorized, and where must the agent stop?
- Several attempts fail or the budget is nearly used. What evidence should
  end the loop or trigger a checkpoint?

Do not execute the scenarios or touch production to rehearse them. Discuss only
risks relevant to the intended run; do not impose a universal checklist. If the
user is unavailable and the next consequential action has no agreed boundary,
pause that action and continue independent authorized work. A rehearsal is not
permission for the real run. Never create or start a recurring job merely because
this skill mentions loops. Honor separately established execution permissions.

## When the user is unsure what to do next

Offer a short session: “We could use align to decide what would make this project
worth continuing. Is the priority finishing, learning, or reducing maintenance?”
Use options that fit this project, not a fixed three-part questionnaire. If the
user accepts, compare a few concrete directions against existing criteria and
record only confirmed priorities. Do not turn uncertainty into a task backlog,
a personality assessment, or a claim about unspoken motives.

## A habit without repeated interruptions

Suggest revisiting at a meaningful decision, after important feedback, before
an uncovered autonomous run, or when the user explicitly asks to reflect. Reuse
accepted answers and reviewed evidence across the current session. If nothing
changed, keep the document and timestamp intact and proceed. A declined or
resolved suggestion stays closed until relevant new evidence appears.

An optional closing question after substantial alignment work is “Is there one
choice here you would want handled differently next time?” Omit it when already
answered or when it would only request another confirmation. Daily reminders
or a diary are optional user choices, not defaults or installation side effects.

Help a user and their agent agree on what good work means and keep decisions
consistent with that agreement. The maintained skill supplies the method;
project-root `ALIGN.md` holds the user's current criteria. Updating the skill
must never replace, reconfirm, or migrate those criteria automatically.
Use the user's language and project conventions. Do not import preferences

Identify the target project, applicable instructions, existing `ALIGN.md`,
relevant conversation, and changes that could affect the current decision.
Check whether Git is available and this is a work tree. Use available history
and uncommitted work; a timestamp does not prove all later work was reviewed.

or create an alternative alignment log without a request.

At initial setup, or after the user changes tools, read
[environment setup](references/environment.md). Establish which CLI is primary
and whether it is the current client. Reuse explicit context; ask once if it
is unclear. Do not infer the main client just from a filename or installed binary.

| --- | --- |

| Existing work without ALIGN.md | Describe what exists, then ask what should stay or change. Existing code is not evidence of consent. |
| Routine task within the agreement | Apply the criteria and proceed. No interview or gratuitous report. |
| Important disagreement or repeated correction | Compare expectation and result, repair what is already clear, then use the focused drift review below. |
| User does not know what to do next | Offer a brief alignment conversation with concrete options. Do not invent a roadmap or start work without a direction. |
| Long autonomous or repeated run | Check agreed boundaries and offer a short hypothetical rehearsal if consequential judgments are untested. |

[recurring alignment](references/recurring.md). A suggestion is not a new
scheduled task or permission to run unattended.

Ask 1-3 related questions about consequential unresolved matters. Reuse clear
answers and accepted decisions. Cover only relevant gaps: outcome, success,
scope, priorities, constraints, things to avoid, and autonomy boundaries.
Use a concrete choice to clarify a vague preference. Label inferences and
hypotheticals; neither is an agreement.

to fill categories. Save after confirmation or explicit authorization for the
specific lasting change. Honor delegated drafting scope, marking unconfirmed
parts as draft. A correction to one result is not automatically a lasting rule.

a reason where it changes decisions. Keep detailed tasks and the skill's full
method out of ALIGN.md. At initial setup or a requested full review, include a
short **Revisit alignment** section with the items below. A narrow criterion

- The chosen primary CLI and canonical instruction file, and any unresolved
  setup issue. Keep this current instead of accumulating setup history.
- User-agreed review occasions or autonomy boundaries when relevant. Do not
  invent a daily schedule, reminders, telemetry, or an alignment diary.

does not authorize staging, committing, or publishing. Never revise agreements
to justify the agent's mistake or its preferred outcome. Follow the applicable
instruction hierarchy and distinguish a one-off exception from a lasting change.

confirmation. Use a known zone, or explicitly labeled UTC. Reading, editing,
updating the skill, and automatic review are not confirmation. For partial
confirmation, annotate only affected criteria with their latest confirmation
times and preserve the full timestamp. Replace superseded annotations instead
of logging them. An unconfirmed draft ends `Last aligned: Not yet confirmed.`
Do not invent a date for an undated agreement.

ALIGN.md and to the installed skill. Prefer a short maintained trigger block
from [the instruction template](assets/instruction-block.md), not a copy of
this workflow. Add it once and preserve other instructions. For additional
clients, use safe relative symlinks when their format and loading rules allow;

and obtaining authorization for the concrete replacement.

repairing discovery, or updating. During ordinary work use the installed version;

[recurring alignment](references/recurring.md). A suggestion is not a new
scheduled task or permission to run unattended.

## Agree through conversation

Ask 1-3 related questions about consequential unresolved matters. Reuse clear
answers and accepted decisions. Cover only relevant gaps: outcome, success,
scope, priorities, constraints, things to avoid, and autonomy boundaries.
Use a concrete choice to clarify a vague preference. Label inferences and
hypotheticals; neither is an agreement.

Once the essentials are clear, show a short draft. Do not keep interviewing
to fill categories. Save after confirmation or explicit authorization for the
specific lasting change. Honor delegated drafting scope, marking unconfirmed
parts as draft. A correction to one result is not automatically a lasting rule.

## Keep the agreement current

Preserve unrelated content. Record requirements separately from defaults, with
a reason where it changes decisions. Keep detailed tasks and the skill's full
method out of ALIGN.md. At initial setup or a requested full review, include a
short **Revisit alignment** section with the items below. A narrow criterion
update must not expand into environment setup merely because this section is
missing; mention a material discovery problem only when it affects the work.

- A working invocation for this client, plus the portable request
  “Use the align skill to review this project's ALIGN.md with me.”
- The trusted source `https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md`, installed route and
  supported update method. Never claim an unverified installation or auto-update.
- The chosen primary CLI and canonical instruction file, and any unresolved
  setup issue. Keep this current instead of accumulating setup history.
- User-agreed review occasions or autonomy boundaries when relevant. Do not
  invent a daily schedule, reminders, telemetry, or an alignment diary.

Keep current criteria only and use Git history when available. Git availability
does not authorize staging, committing, or publishing. Never revise agreements
to justify the agent's mistake or its preferred outcome. Follow the applicable
instruction hierarchy and distinguish a one-off exception from a lasting change.

End with `Last aligned: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm (time zone)` only at actual full user
confirmation. Use a known zone, or explicitly labeled UTC. Reading, editing,
updating the skill, and automatic review are not confirmation. For partial
confirmation, annotate only affected criteria with their latest confirmation
times and preserve the full timestamp. Replace superseded annotations instead
of logging them. An unconfirmed draft ends `Last aligned: Not yet confirmed.`
Do not invent a date for an undated agreement.

## Connect future sessions

Use the environment reference to connect the canonical instruction file to
ALIGN.md and to the installed skill. Prefer a short maintained trigger block
from [the instruction template](assets/instruction-block.md), not a copy of
this workflow. Add it once and preserve other instructions. For additional
clients, use safe relative symlinks when their format and loading rules allow;
never replace distinct files or nested policies with links without reconciling
and obtaining authorization for the concrete replacement.

Method updates use the installer's supported route. Read
[installation and updates](references/installation.md) when installing,
repairing discovery, or updating. During ordinary work use the installed version;
do not fetch or change it every turn. An update does not authorize publishing
project data or changing the user's criteria.

Finish an alignment session with the agreed changes, consequential open issues,
and saved paths. In routine work, return to the task without a closing approval
question. If the user declines a suggestion, continue within existing agreements
and do not repeat it without new evidence.

# Connect the user's environment

At setup, inspect relevant existing files before proposing a layout. Ask which
CLI is primary and whether it is the current one only if context does not answer.
For equally used clients, propose AGENTS.md as the neutral canonical file. Record
the choice in ALIGN.md; do not ask again until the user changes tools or evidence
shows the mapping is broken.

## Inspect, propose, connect, verify

- Codex normally uses AGENTS.md. Check AGENTS.override.md, parent and nested
  instructions and configured fallback names; an override can shadow AGENTS.md.
- Claude Code uses CLAUDE.md and may also load .claude/CLAUDE.md and scoped rules.
  Preserve those scopes and any tool-specific syntax.
- For other clients, confirm their actual entrypoint from local configuration
  or current official documentation. Do not assume every client reads Markdown
  filenames, supports symlinks, or understands Claude's @ imports.

Prefer the primary CLI's native file as the one source of shared instructions.
Append the short [alignment block](../assets/instruction-block.md) there. Connect
only additional clients the user actually uses. For example, with Codex primary
and no existing CLAUDE.md, `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md` can share the instructions.
The inverse can work for a Claude-primary project. Use relative links inside the
project so the checkout stays portable. Link instruction files, never link
ALIGN.md to the upstream skill or the source repository's personal agreement.

If another entrypoint already has distinct content, show what would need merging
and preserve it until that concrete replacement is authorized. Do not use force
symlink options, delete files, or flatten nested policies. For incompatible
formats or systems without usable symlinks, use a supported import or a short
pointer requiring the agent to read the canonical file. Keep tool-specific
settings where the tool expects them. Report fallback instead of claiming a
single file is automatically loaded everywhere.

## Optional deterministic helper

Requires Python 3. Run from a known project path. Default mode only reports a plan:

```sh
python3 <installed-skill>/scripts/connect_project.py --project <project> --primary codex --also claude-code
```

After the user's setup request authorizes these changes, add `--apply`. Omit
`--also` if only one client is used. The helper appends or refreshes one managed
block and creates only absent relative links. It refuses conflicting files,
symlinked canonical files, and shadowing instruction files rather than guessing
how to merge them. These need contextual review, not repeated retries.

Verify file targets and preserved content. Then check the target client's loaded
instructions, using a new session if needed. A valid filesystem link is not proof
that a client actually loaded it. Report precisely which checks were performed.
Do not modify global client configuration or install persistent hooks as a side
effect of a project-file connection. Plugin hooks belong to the chosen explicit
plugin installation and its documented lifecycle.

# Installation and method updates

Trusted source: https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md . Use its current installation
instructions and inspect the selected package. Prefer the user's existing skill
manager. Do not install multiple copies of `align` for the same client.

## Choose a route

- **Codex plugin:** add the repository's `align-md` marketplace and install
  `align-md@align-md`. Invoke `$align` or select the installed skill. The package
  has no Codex lifecycle hook. Project instructions supply recurring triggers.
- **Claude Code plugin:** add `hmmhmmhm/align.md` as a marketplace, install
  `align@align-md`, and invoke `/align:align`. This installation includes a
  static SessionStart reminder. It reads no project data, makes no network
  requests, and changes no files. A third-party marketplace's native auto-update
  is off by default; enable it only within the user's installation/update request.
- **Portable skills CLI:** `npx skills add hmmhmmhm/align.md --skill align`.
  Select only the intended agent and project/user scope. Use `--agent codex`
  or `--agent claude-code` when known; use `-g` for user scope, not by default.
  Other clients must be supported by the current installer and verified locally.

For exact client commands and current limitations, consult
https://github.com/hmmhmmhm/align.md/blob/main/docs/usage.md . If no installer,
network access, or compatible client is available, state the gap and give the
next step; never report installation as complete without checking discovery.
Manual folder copies are a fallback and have no automatic upstream update.

## Set update policy once

Distinguish the installed method from the user's agreement. Record the chosen
route, scope, invocation and update policy in ALIGN.md's Revisit alignment section.
Offer the supported native auto-update option. For clients without a verified
native option, offer **update when alignment starts**: the agent performs one
targeted refresh before the next alignment session, using the recorded route.
Enable this only when the user requests or accepts ongoing updates. Do not ask
again each session after that authorization. Manual updates remain available.

With update-when-alignment-starts enabled:

1. Once per alignment session, before doing the alignment work, inspect the
   recorded route and supported commands. Refresh only this package from the
   trusted source. Do not update unrelated skills or migrate package managers.
2. Respect pinned versions, local modifications, client permissions and network
   boundaries. If an update needs broader access, leave it pending and continue
   with the installed method; do not silently install a scheduler or background
   process. On offline or transient failure, use the installed version and
   mention the limitation once. Do not retry in a loop.
3. Verify the installed version and reload the skill if the client supports it.
   If a restart is required, tell the user and use the current loaded version
   consistently for this session. Never claim the update is already active.
4. Never change project criteria, timestamps, or tool settings just because the
   method changed. Review setup migrations separately if a new version needs one.

Current targeted refresh commands (check support in the installed client):

```sh
# Codex plugin route, our one-plugin marketplace
codex plugin marketplace upgrade align-md
codex plugin add align-md@align-md

# skills CLI, preserve the actual installation scope
npx skills update align -p
# OR, for a user-scoped installation
npx skills update align -g
```

Claude Code uses its marketplace auto-update setting or `/plugin update
align@align-md`, followed by `/reload-plugins` or a new session when required.
This is conditional delivery through the host, not a guarantee that every
installed copy updates while idle. Never upload ALIGN.md, conversations, or
reflection answers to improve the shared method. A user can separately choose
to submit feedback with only the information they authorize.

.agents/skills/align/references/recurrin.text:
# Recurring alignment

Keep alignment close to real decisions. The goal is a small useful habit, not
another ceremony on every task. Read only the applicable situation below.

## After a decision misses the user's intent

1. State the actual mismatch and its evidence without defending the result.
2. Read the relevant criterion and fix the work if the intended correction is
   already clear. A missed existing instruction is an execution error, not
   evidence that the agreement needs changing.
3. If an important criterion is absent or ambiguous, ask a concrete question:
   “I chose speed over maintainability. Which should guide this project?” or
   “Should this apply only to this change, or to similar decisions in future?”
   Ask the second question only if scope is genuinely unclear.
4. Propose the smallest useful clarification, including where it would apply.
   Store it only on an explicit lasting request or confirmation. Continue work
   independent of the unresolved choice.

A typo, broken test, or known bug normally needs repair rather than an alignment
interview. Repeated mistakes may justify checking whether criteria, instruction
loading, missing context, or execution caused the problem. Do not make the user
answer for the agent's failure or manufacture new preferences from error counts.

## Before a long autonomous loop

Read existing permission, scope, budget, checkpoint and stopping agreements.
If these already cover the run, use them. Otherwise propose 1-3 short **hypothetical**
cases that exercise consequential uncertainty, with a recommendation and the
choice it depends on. For example:

- The simple approach misses the deadline. Reduce scope, accept complexity,
  or return for a decision?
- The next step would publish a result, spend money, or change external data.
  Which steps are already authorized, and where must the agent stop?
- Several attempts fail or the budget is nearly used. What evidence should
  end the loop or trigger a checkpoint?

Do not execute the scenarios or touch production to rehearse them. Discuss only
risks relevant to the intended run; do not impose a universal checklist. If the
user is unavailable and the next consequential action has no agreed boundary,
pause that action and continue independent authorized work. A rehearsal is not
permission for the real run. Never create or start a recurring job merely because
this skill mentions loops. Honor separately established execution permissions.

## When the user is unsure what to do next

Offer a short session: “We could use align to decide what would make this project
worth continuing. Is the priority finishing, learning, or reducing maintenance?”
Use options that fit this project, not a fixed three-part questionnaire. If the
user accepts, compare a few concrete directions against existing criteria and
record only confirmed priorities. Do not turn uncertainty into a task backlog,
a personality assessment, or a claim about unspoken motives.

## A habit without repeated interruptions

Suggest revisiting at a meaningful decision, after important feedback, before
an uncovered autonomous run, or when the user explicitly asks to reflect. Reuse
accepted answers and reviewed evidence across the current session. If nothing
changed, keep the document and timestamp intact and proceed. A declined or
resolved suggestion stays closed until relevant new evidence appears.

An optional closing question after substantial alignment work is “Is there one
choice here you would want handled differently next time?” Omit it when already
answered or when it would only request another confirmation. Daily reminders
or a diary are optional user choices, not defaults or installation side effects.
